correctness.rationale: For any stable alternative changing m pairs, proposer optimality makes each switched man strictly worse, so his utility ratio is at most (n-1)/n, with equality only from first to second. Each switched woman's ratio is at most n, with equality only from last to first. The resulting (n-1)^m bound, positivity and m<=n give the claimed bound and the universal n=2 factor one. For n>=3 equality forces m=n and all stipulated ranks. Disjoint perfect matchings can realize those ranks, one stable by all men's top choices and the other by all women's top choices. Each man has a unique second choice, so the Nash maximizer is unique at equality. The matchings and residual list orders give the stated labeled count without duplication and division by (n!)^(2n) gives the probability. Mutual first choices in a bijection force the only stable matching and attain the lower bound. An independent exhaustive replay obtained factors 1 and 8, with 16 and 12 extremal profiles for n=2 and n=3, respectively, and checked the n=3 extremizer ranks and uniqueness.
residual_risks: The enumeration covers only n=2 and n=3; the proof, not the replay, establishes all n.
